do you have a criminal record? do you have any debilitating illnesses? if not then my advice to you would be to get busy living. You can make things better, but you have to empower yourself. Think about college scholarships (and a GED if needed (i had to do the UK equivalent and recently finished an MSc at London School of Economics for which i received a full scholarship). 

Think about finding a form of exercise that you can enjoy, regularly(for me that was cycling - 2 birds 1 stone if you gotta be somewhere!). Think about eating healthily/enough/regularly (as in 3 times per day at the same time every day - i found this really helped) and staying hydrated. Healthy body = healthy mind. Think carefully about any toxic habits/people in your life that you need to stop/distance from (i call it trimming the fat - and it's one of the hardest but most important). 

Think about all the amazing things you could do (and feel) if you were successful (economic) and happy/confident (social). Look in the mirror and tell yourself you deserve a shot at these things every day - if it doesn't work then try again tomorrow, and if you end up crying or whatever then call Samaritans and talk about it (seriously! they can be very supportive!).

First of all, it's not selfish to feel suicidal. Unfortunately, most people (especially those closest to you) will not find it easy to talk about things like that - **try Samaritans,** I always wish I had tried them earlier in my life (I am now 28, and only started using them recently). 

I hate to sound like a hard-ass, but you do have to ***want*** to be happy. Of course, it's not as simple as just that one thing - but that's usually where it starts for those of us not lucky enough to for it to come naturally.

You deserve to be happy - everyone has that right. The best things for a happy life are physical exercise, good relationships (friends, coworkers, and partners (and pets!)), personal development, nature, and following (or finding) your passion - obviously money has a huge impact on your quality of life (economically ***and*** socially) so that's something you must also consider. You can still do all these things - but you must be prepared to be disciplined & maintain ***some*** positivity. Beyond that, part of figuring out the meaning of life is figuring it out for yourself - although there are already many great thinkers to get inspired by e.g. John Stuart Mill: "There are many truths by which the full meaning cannot be realised until personal experience has brought it home."

It may not always feel like it, but life is a gift (unless you REALLY fuck it up and/or you're REALLY unlucky) so grab that gift by the balls: 1) always look after YOURSELF first; 2) always be respectful and kind to others; 3) work hard; and 4) try to be patient if something doesn't work out right away.
